stories.title: Trump and Xi Jinping to meet in Washington
stories.details: President Trump and President Xi are set to meet to discuss trade and artificial intelligence. While the meeting signals high-level concern, both nations remain skeptical of slowing AI development, with Trump emphasizing the need to maintain US dominance.

stories.title: Trump praises UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham
stories.details: In their first meeting at the UN, President Trump praised Andy Burnham as a 'natural businessperson' and noted improved relations. However, Trump remained critical of the UK's decision to hand over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran at UN General Assembly
stories.details: President Trump delivered a combative speech at the UN, threatening to 'annihilate' Iran if a deal regarding their nuclear program is not reached. Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian, is expected to address the assembly later.

stories.title: New UK agency to fight 'information warfare'
stories.details: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the creation of a new UK agency tasked with countering 'information warfare' from hostile states like Russia. The announcement was made during his visit to the UN.

stories.title: AI doomsday warnings spark global debate
stories.details: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, warning that AI could kill humanity by the end of the decade. His claims have gained significant traction, prompting calls for regulation and safety testing across the US and EU.

stories.title: OpenAI solves 100+ open math problems
stories.details: OpenAI announced its internal model has solved over 100 previously unsolved math problems. The company is establishing an independent advisory group to oversee how these results are assessed and announced.

stories.title: Xiaomi's new AI model tops open benchmarks
stories.details: Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro has become the strongest openly available AI model. The company claims it achieved this through expanded reinforcement learning, though it faces scrutiny over training data sources.

stories.title: Meta patches Muse exploit
stories.details: Meta quickly patched a zero-day flaw in its Muse app that allowed attackers to hijack user accounts and access sensitive files. Security researchers criticized the company for failing to build in adequate security from the start.

stories.title: Oil prices fall amid supply hopes
stories.details: Oil prices have dropped for a sixth consecutive session, falling below $100 a barrel. The decline is driven by reports of increased supply from the Middle East and progress in US-Iran talks.

stories.title: Jim Ratcliffe halts production at Hull chemical plants
stories.details: Ineos, led by Sir Jim Ratcliffe, is mothballing three chemical plants in Hull. The decision follows what the company describes as 'ridiculously high' gas prices in the UK.

stories.title: UK borrows £18bn in August
stories.details: The UK government borrowed £18 billion in August, placing significant pressure on Chancellor Healey ahead of the upcoming budget. The figures highlight the ongoing fiscal challenges facing the administration.

stories.title: European drugmakers losing ground
stories.details: European pharmaceutical companies report they are losing competitive ground to their US and Chinese rivals. The industry is calling for more support to maintain its position in the global market.

stories.title: Fifa president Infantino faces pressure
stories.details: Fifa president Gianni Infantino is facing intense scrutiny and attempts to oust him following the controversial sell-off of World Cup broadcasting rights. Critics are questioning his leadership and future at the organization.

stories.title: England takes lead in ODI cricket series
stories.details: England secured a victory in the first match of their ODI series against Sri Lanka. The win was highlighted by a strong bowling performance, with the team winning by 89 runs.

stories.title: British swimming team targets cross-Channel record
stories.details: A team of British swimmers is attempting to break a 36-year-old cross-Channel swimming record. The team is battling difficult conditions, including strong tides, waves, and jellyfish.

stories.title: Thinktank calls for abolition of state pension
stories.details: A thinktank linked to the Reform UK party has proposed the abolition of the state pension. The suggestion has sparked significant debate regarding the future of social security in the UK.

stories.title: Conservatives draw level with Reform UK
stories.details: A new poll shows the Conservative Party has drawn level with Reform UK for the first time in 18 months. The shift is seen as a boost for party leader Kemi Badenoch.

stories.title: Call to end 'sicknote culture'
stories.details: Proposals have been made to require employees to speak directly to managers when calling in sick. The move aims to end what some describe as an 'insidious' sicknote culture in the workplace.
